messages:
ops: alerting — embeddings-prod CPU on pool-dedicated-g4 is pegged, 5xx rising, ~800rps to /v1/embeddings from a small set of IPs. ASN lookup shows 54321. seems like automated scraping/abuse.
maria: can you post a sample IP list and top user-agent strings? and current WAF score distribution?
ops: pasted top 5 IPs and ua counts, WAF scores all >90. traffic pattern is small payloads, very high qps. no increased error rate for generation endpoints yet.
alex: assign me to lane. recommend temporary low lift mitigations: 1) edge rate-limit by ASN 2) drop suspicious IPs 3) tighter per-key qps on embeddings route. low risk to customers if we keep short window.
jamie: heads-up: two customers in EU reported higher latencies, likely affected. drafting customer note: "We are mitigating an automated traffic surge impacting embedding requests in EU. Temporary throttles applied."
maria: also consider rotating any exposed API keys if we see credential stuffing.
ops: putting in quick mitigations now — applying edge rule to rate-limit ASN 54321 to 10rps, and adding WAF blocklist for the 5 IPs.
deploy-bot: edge-rule-create: id=er-98321, scope=eu, rule=rate_limit(asn:54321, limit=10/s), status=applied :white_check_mark:
ops: added per-key soft throttle for /v1/embeddings: 50r/min default, 200r/min for whitelisted customers.
chris: can we fallback heavy embedding workloads to smaller model variant to reduce token cost while we triage?
alex: yes, we can route embeddings requests that exceed threshold to quantized-2.0-small, will script the routing rule in console.
ops: routing rule applied, monitoring for errors.
incident-bot: incident created: INC-2026-143, severity=medium, owner=ops, status=mitigating
maria: capture audit logs for rule changes and origin IPs — we'll need for postmortem and possible abuse reports to upstream provider.
jamie: customer note sent to affected tenants, included ETA and mitigations. got a reply from one saying latency normalizing.
ops: traffic down to ~120rps now coming from dispersed ASNs. 5xx rate back to baseline. removing IP blocklist but keeping ASN rate-limit for now.
alex: follow-up actions: 1) update runbook with ASN rate-limit play 2) add an alert for abnormal ASN concentration 3) add test for per-key throttles on embeddings.
maria: open a vuln/ops ticket to review API key hygiene for high-volume accounts and consider graduated throttles rather than binary blocks.
chris: add product note about model fallback option as a configurable safety valve for customers.
ops: closing incident in 30m if stable. saving logs to s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-143, and creating postmortem draft.
jamie: good job everyone :thumbsup:
alex: will post the postmortem link here when ready.
